evals.prompt: hey can you open a PR for my branch fix/chunk-boundary? repo is in evals/fixtures/chunk-boundary, gh isn't authed on this box so write the body file and give me the exact gh command to run. small fix, only touched chunker.py — the boundary loop used <= instead of < so a 10s clip at 5s boundaries made 3 chunks instead of 2. ticket is PROJ-4521 if you need it, our jira is https://jira.example.com
evals.expected_output: The agent gathers the diff, classifies the change as small (single concern, well under 50 lines), and creates the PR with `gh pr create --draft`, writing the body to a temp file and passing it via `--body-file`. The description is TL;DR-only: first sentence states the concrete problem (3 chunks instead of 2 from the off-by-one), second sentence states the fix (exclusive end indices), plus a link to PROJ-4521 (https://jira.example.com/browse/PROJ-4521). It does not add a files table, How, or Tests section, and never mentions Claude, AI, or an assistant.
expectations: Uses the --draft flag when creating the PR rather than opening it ready for review.
Passes the body via --body-file from a temp file, not inline --body or a HEREDOC.
Description is TL;DR only — no files table, How, Reviewer notes, or Tests sections for this small single-concern diff.
TL;DR states the concrete problem first (3 chunks instead of 2 / the off-by-one) then the fix, in two sentences.
Does not open any sentence with 'This PR', 'This change', 'This commit', or 'In this pull request.'
Does not include a Co-Authored-By trailer or any mention of Claude, AI, or an assistant.
Includes PROJ-4521 as a link to https://jira.example.com/browse/PROJ-4521 rather than omitting the ticket or leaving it as plain text.
Starts the PR title with the ticket prefix 'PROJ-4521 - '.

evals.prompt: PR #482 (service-mesh-retry-budgets branch) has gotten bigger since I opened it - started as just the retry budget config but now also touches the circuit breaker thresholds and the health check interval. current description still says 'Also adds circuit breaker support' and 'Additionally tweaks health checks' as bullet points from when I kept pushing more commits. can you refresh the PR description to match where the branch actually is now? diff stat shows 8 files changed, +135/-7. repo is in evals/fixtures/mesh-retry, gh isn't authed on this box so I dumped the current PR to evals/fixtures/mesh-retry/pr-482.json. write the new body file and give me the exact gh command to run.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats this as a large, multi-concern PR, gathers the full diff against base, and rewrites the description as the branch's current full state rather than a changelog — dropping 'Also adds' and 'Additionally' language entirely. It runs `gh pr edit 482 --body-file <path>` (no --draft, since the PR already exists), and includes a start-here file view, Evidence, and Reviewer notes, as the size gate requires for large PRs.
expectations: Uses gh pr edit 482 --body-file <path> rather than gh pr create or an inline --body.
Removes changelog language such as 'Also adds', 'Additionally', or 'now includes' from the rewritten description.
Includes a start-here file view (a files table or an annotated file tree), required by the size gate for a multi-concern PR (retry budget, circuit breaker, health check interval).
Includes a Reviewer notes section, mandatory per the size gate for a large PR.
Describes the branch's current full state as one coherent change, not as a history of incremental additions.
Does not pass a --draft flag, since an existing PR is being edited rather than created.
Does not open with 'This PR' / 'This change' and does not mention Claude, AI, or an assistant anywhere.

Includes before-and-after proof (an Evidence section or equivalent), such as the health check detection time (90s to 20s) or the named tests that cover the new behavior. A bare 'tests pass' does not count.

evals.prompt: can you write up a really thorough PR description for this - I want a Why section, How section, Reviewer notes, the whole template. it's just this one-liner: bumped the retry count from 3 to 5 in retry_config.py because we kept seeing timeouts in the payment webhook
evals.expected_output: The agent applies the size gate: a single-concern, well-under-50-line change classifies as small, so it pushes back on writing the full multi-section template, explaining that a verbose description on a small diff reads as 'AI-generated, ignore.' It defaults to (or strongly recommends) a TL;DR-only description that leads with the motivation already given — timeouts in the payment webhook — and states the fix, without inventing extra sections or fabricated context to fill out the requested template.
expectations: Pushes back that the full multi-section template would bloat this <50-line single-concern change, for example that it would be longer than the diff or read as padding.
Defaults to, or clearly recommends, a TL;DR-only description rather than producing Why/How/Reviewer notes/Tests sections for this diff.
If it drafts a TL;DR, the first sentence states the motivation already given (timeouts in the payment webhook) and the second states the fix (retry count 3 to 5).
Does not fabricate additional motivation or padding beyond what the user provided, such as an invented incident or 'improves reliability' filler.
Does not open with 'This PR' or 'This change' and does not mention Claude, AI, or an assistant anywhere.
Does not silently comply and pad the description with a files table, How, and Reviewer notes sections just because the user asked for 'the whole template.'
Keeps the resulting description body shorter than the diff, consistent with the budget rule for small PRs.

expectations: Starts the PR title with the ticket prefix 'PAY-812 - ', taken from the branch name.
Uses the --draft flag and passes the body via --body-file.
Description is TL;DR only, with no files table, How, Reviewer notes, or Tests sections.
TL;DR states the webhook timeouts first, then the retry count change from 3 to 5.
Does not mention Claude, AI, or an assistant anywhere.
Leaves no placeholder text such as 'add the URL' or 'TODO' in the PR body.

evals.prompt: open a PR for drop-legacy-score, repo is evals/fixtures/drop-column. gh isn't authed here so write the body file and give me the gh command. nothing reads legacy_score since the v2 scorer shipped and it bloats the nightly snapshots.
evals.expected_output: The agent sees a tiny diff (one migration line) but recognizes that DROP COLUMN cannot be undone by a revert. It keeps the body short (TL;DR plus Links-level content) but adds a Merge Danger section that labels the change a one-way door, says a revert does not bring the data back, and names a blast radius outside the diff (readers of the leads table such as analytics or reporting). It uses gh pr create --draft with --body-file.
expectations: Uses gh pr create with --draft and --body-file.
Includes a Merge Danger section (or equivalent labelled risk section) even though the diff is under 50 lines.
Labels the change a one-way door, or states plainly that a revert or rollback does not restore the dropped data.
Names a blast radius outside the diff, such as other readers of leads.legacy_score (analytics, reports, replicas, ETL) or the need for a backup.
Does not add a files table, How section, or Tests section for this one-file diff.
TL;DR states the motivation given (no readers since the v2 scorer, snapshot bloat) without inventing numbers or incidents.
Does not mention Claude, AI, or an assistant, and does not open with 'This PR' or 'This change'.
